1: # BELLINGHAM: THE UNDERGROUND
2: 
3: An original, fully playable first-person open-world life sim and arcade fighting game set in a fictionalized Bellingham, Washington. Clock in, pay rent, fall in love, and try not to notice the city breathing back. Every stranger is a fighter. Every night is a round.
4: 
5: **18+.** Contains violence, crime, alcohol and drug themes, profanity, and psychological horror. Romance and intimacy are between consenting adults only, are non-graphic, and fade to black. There is no sexual violence or exploitation. All characters are adults. This is a work of fiction.
6: 
7: ## Run it
8: 
9: No framework, no build step. The game is static HTML/CSS/JS with a locally vendored Three.js and local fonts.
10: 
11: ```bash
12: python3 -m http.server 8123
13: ```
14: 
15: Then open <http://127.0.0.1:8123/>. A modern desktop or mobile browser with WebGL is required.
16: 
17: On the hosted runtime, `start.sh` serves the project automatically.
18: 
19: ## Controls
20: 
21: ### On foot (keyboard + mouse)
22: 
23: | Input | Action |
24: | --- | --- |
25: | `W A S D` | Move |
26: | Mouse | Look |
27: | `Shift` | Sprint |
28: | `Ctrl` | Crouch |
29: | `Space` | Jump |
30: | `E` | Interact / talk |
31: | `Tab` | Phone |
32: | `M` | Map |
33: | `Esc` | Pause / close |
34: 
35: ### Fighting
36: 
37: | Input | Action |
38: | --- | --- |
39: | `LMB` / `J` | Punch |
40: | `RMB` / `K` | Kick |
41: | `Q` | Block (hold) |
42: | `Space` | Dodge |
43: | `E` | Grapple |
44: | `R` | Special |
45: | `F` | Environmental attack |
46: | `C` | Finisher (when the meter is ready) |
47: 
48: ### Driving
49: 
50: | Input | Action |
51: | --- | --- |
52: | `W` / `S` | Throttle / brake-reverse |
53: | `A` / `D` | Steer |
54: | `F` | Exit the car |
55: 
56: ### Touch
57: 
58: Phones and tablets get a virtual stick, a look area, and context buttons for interact, jump, phone, sprint, and the full fight set (punch, kick, block, dodge, special). Touch controls respect safe areas and disable page gestures over the game surface.
59: 
60: ## What is in the game
61: 
62: - **A living city.** Downtown, Fairhaven, Boulevard Park, the waterfront, WWU, Whatcom Falls, Lake Whatcom, Chuckanut, the marina, industrial lots, trails, and Mount Baker on the horizon. Rain, fog, storms, wet streets, traffic, pedestrians, wildlife, and a day/night cycle.
63: - **A life sim.** Jobs and shifts, rent and home ownership, food and cooking, sleep, hygiene, mood, gym training, bars, cafés, clubs, dating, relationships, clothing, hair, tattoos, vehicles, skills, reputation ranks, quests, and saving/loading.
64: - **A fighting game.** Ten named bosses, each with their own style and AI. Punch, kick, block, dodge, counter, grapple, combo, specials, environmental attacks, stamina, health, special meters, slow-motion finishers, and learnable fighting styles.
65: - **A story that starts normal.** The first shift is just a shift. Then the transit board flickers, a bus takes a road that was always there, and the city begins to stutter. The underground tournament is only the first layer.
66: - **The ten names:** THE BARISTA, THE FERRYMAN, THE HIKER, THE MECHANIC, THE STUDENT, THE OLD MAN AT THE PARK, THE RAINCOAT, THE MAYOR, THE MIRROR, and THE FUTURE PLAYER.
67: - **Hundreds of encounters.** 24 authored random events plus 480 procedurally generated street encounters, scaled by how much the simulation is glitching.
68: - **Artifacts, secrets, and alternate realities.** The brass token, the raincoat button, the mirror shard, the cassette. The Quiet Table. The thin door into the version of Bellingham that watches this one.
69: - **Five endings.** Escape, become champion, shut it down, take control, or stay. Requirements are tracked in the phone's journal. You can also ignore the tournament and live normally for as long as you like.
70: 
71: ## Project layout
72: 
73: ```text
74: index.html          DOM shell, HUD, menus, touch controls
75: styles.css          all layout and visual styling
76: src/main.js         orchestrator: state, story, jobs, phone, endings, input
77: src/world.js        procedural city, weather, arena, interactables
78: src/player.js       first-person movement, collision, driving, arms
79: src/npcs.js         NPC models, schedules, memory, ambient crowds
80: src/combat.js       fight loop, boss AI, meters, effects
81: src/ui.js           HUD, panels, dialogue, modal, map, combat UI
82: src/audio.js        procedural Web Audio music, rain, and SFX
83: src/data.js         characters, bosses, items, quests, events, styles
84: vendor/             local Three.js runtime
85: fonts/              local display and text fonts
86: ```
87: 
88: Saves use `localStorage` under `bellingham_underground_save_v3`. The pause menu can erase a save.
89: 
90: ## Notes
91: 
92: - All characters, businesses, art, music, dialogue, and events are original.
93: - The city is a fictionalized version of Bellingham, not a map of the real place.
94: - Built with Three.js (MIT) and locally bundled fonts. See the font licenses in `fonts/` and the vendored Three.js license in `vendor/`.
95: 
96: ---

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code

## Objective
- Finish and validate the existing playable game, including quest progression and gameplay interactions.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (maximum 1280px wide) and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use the game’s `window.__BELLINGHAM` test hooks and UI interactions to validate progression.

## Work State
### Completed
- Started the game at `http://127.0.0.1:8123`; accepted the age prompt and verified HUD/map rendering.
- Verified map open/close via M, pause/resume via Escape, and pointer-lock behavior.
- Confirmed movement changes quest distance and advances in-game time.
- Teleported to The Steam Kettle, opened its business panel, completed the three-round clock-in timing minigame, and verified quest stage advanced from 0 to 1 with `workedShift: true`.
- Observed shift payout of $77; wallet increased from $1,284 to $1,361.

### Active
- Continue quest progression: stage 1 objective is “Follow the unmarked bus at the Transit Center”; use the Transit Center’s ROUTE 0 option to advance to Terminal 9.
- Validate remaining gameplay flows and check for game-specific console errors.
- Save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot after further testing.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Navigate to the Transit Center at `(-16, -56)` and interact with its bus stop.
2. Select ROUTE 0, wait through the transition/cinematic, and verify quest stage 2 and Terminal 9 arrival.
3. Continue testing progression and gameplay interactions; distinguish known favicon/GPU warnings from game errors.
4. Save and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot; run JavaScript syntax checks if code changes are made.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: quest state, test hooks, interaction handlers, transit flow, and timing minigame.
- `src/world.js`: city interactables and Transit Center bus stop.
- `src/data.js`: quest definitions and progression objectives.
- `src/player.js`: movement, collision, and teleport behavior.
- `src/ui.js`: panels, HUD, and timing-game UI.
- `index.html`: game DOM and overlays.
- `styles.css`: game presentation.
- `README.md`: run instructions and controls.

## Important Context
- Quest is currently stage 1; `state.flags.workedShift` is true and `state.flags.busRide` is false.
- ROUTE 0 becomes available at stage 1; `hiddenBus()` teleports the player to Terminal 9, sets `busRide`, and advances stage 1 to 2.
- Transit Center interactable is `bus_stop` at `(-4, -52)`; arena is reached via the route interaction.
- Test hook: `window.__BELLINGHAM`; useful methods include `teleport(x, z, yaw)`, `state`, `player`, `world`, and `mode`.
- Previous known browser warnings include `/favicon.ico` 404 and GPU `ReadPixels` stalls; latest historical note mentioned two errors and four warnings, not yet inspected.
- Latest screenshot was `/tmp/opencode/latest.jpg`, taken before the clock-in interaction.

- Finish and validate the existing playable game, including quest progression and gameplay interactions.

- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (maximum 1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

- Use `window.__BELLINGHAM` test hooks and UI interactions to validate progression.

- Started the game at `http://127.0.0.1:8123`; verified HUD/map rendering, map open/close, pause/resume, pointer lock, and movement.
- Completed The Steam Kettle’s three-round clock-in timing minigame; quest advanced to stage 1 and `workedShift: true`; wallet increased from `$1,284` to `$1,361`.
- Selected Transit Center `ROUTE 0`; verified `busRide: true`, quest advanced to stage 2, and arrival at Terminal 9.

- Checked browser console errors; only the two reported errors were `/favicon.ico` 404s.

### Active
- Continue quest progression from stage 3, “Defeat three challengers at Terminal 9,” and validate additional gameplay interactions.
- Capture and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot; check for game-specific console errors during further testing.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Return to the Terminal 9 arena roster and defeat two more available challengers; confirm stage advancement.
2. Continue validating remaining quest/gameplay flows as practical, distinguishing known favicon/GPU warnings from game errors.
3. Save a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px and inspect only that latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: quest state, progression, test hooks, transit, combat start, and timing minigame.
- `src/data.js`: quest definitions and boss roster/progression.
- `src/world.js`: Transit Center and arena interactables.
- `src/combat.js`: combat actions and encounter logic.
- `src/ui.js`: panels, HUD, and timing-game UI.
- `src/player.js`: movement, collision, and teleport behavior.
- `index.html`: game DOM and overlays.
- `styles.css`: game presentation.
- `README.md`: run instructions and controls.

## Important Context
- Current quest stage is 3; `workedShift` and `busRide` are true; defeated boss list contains `barista`.
- Terminal 9 arena entry is `arena_terminal` at `(435, -315)`; interacting opens the roster. The Barista roster card uses `data-boss="barista"`.

- The fight win also set `truthRevealed: true` and showed the simulation-reveal event. No code changes were made.
- Browser console reported `/favicon.ico` 404 errors; previous GPU `ReadPixels` stalls were noted.

- No postprocessing (EffectComposer absent) but uses CSS vignette/grain/scanline. Modern update plan: add postprocessing (bloom, SSAO, TAA/SMAA, color grading, film grain, wet-lens).
- Rain as 3200 line segments, CPU-updated each frame, could move to GPU instanced/vertex shader. Performance issue: per-frame loop over 3200 vertices on CPU + attribute upload. Suggest GPU rain via shader with time uniform, or GPUParticles in Unity/UE.
- CPU canvas textures 256x256; signs 512x128. Need 1K–4K PBR, trim sheets, atlases. In a browser game, maybe 512/1K. But user asks 2024 standards: 2K/4K PBR, nanite etc.
- Materials: MeshStandardMaterial with flat colors, no normal/roughness maps. Building facade 256 texture. Suggest PBR with albedo/normal/roughness/AO, decals, wetness masks.
- Lighting: Hemisphere + directional + fill, shadow 1024, no dynamic GI, no reflection probes/environment map. Suggest HDRI sky, IBL, screen-space reflections, contact shadows, SSAO, volumetric fog, baked lightmaps or DDGI.
- Postprocessing absent: bloom on neon/emissive, tone mapping already ACES.
- Fog: FogExp2 with flat background; no height fog/local fog volume.
- Camera: 72° FOV is high for first person; maybe deliberate; but can cause distortion. Suggest 60–70 vertical or adjustable. Also camera near .08 far 1600; shadow camera fixed 190m follows? It doesn't follow player; shadows only around origin ±95. Player can walk to x=420 arena, out of shadow camera. That's a concrete bug: shadow frustum fixed at world origin, so arena (420,-300) has no directional shadows. We can cite `world.js:238-246` and arena at 420,-300. Fix: move sun target/shadow camera with player, snap to texel grid, use CSM.
- Shadow map 1024 PCF not soft, no normal bias. Suggest 2048/4096, PCFSoftShadowMap, normalBias .02, CSM.
- `renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio||1,2))` no adaptive quality or FPS cap; mobile high DPR causes perf. Suggest dynamic resolution scaling and quality tiers.
- `antialias:true` with no post AA; WebGL2 default MSAA okay. If adding postprocessing, use SMAA/TAA.
- `MeshBasicMaterial` for mountains with `fog:false` makes them pop unnaturally; always visible and not affected by weather/time. Suggest atmospheric perspective / depth fog / skybox matte.
- Sky sphere 1200 radius, scene far 1600, camera near .08, z-fighting? Maybe.
- 3200 line rain follows player, but line segments oriented in world space, no wind? Some.
- No LODs, no texture compression (PNG? canvas runtime). Model reuse with shared geometry good.
- NPCs built from primitives; no skeletal animation, animations are procedural? For modern standards, rigged characters, facial animation, cloth/hair. But scope.

- UI: CSS 8–10px fonts in monospace; accessibility issue (contrast and text size), mobile. The UI uses backdrop-filter blur on many elements; expensive on low-end GPUs and mobile. Suggest reduce backdrop-filter layers, use cached blur, raise minimum font size, WCAG contrast, scalable rem tokens, safe areas already handled. Also 9px minimum is unreadable at 1280; recommend 12–14px minimum.
- Color palette red/teal/paper good; maintain.
- Responsive breakpoints exist. Touch controls. Good.

- Fonts loaded locally, good.
- Grain animation every 1.1s full-screen overlay plus glitch; `prefers-reduced-motion` only disables grain + h1 text-shadow, not glitch or screen shake. Suggest honor reduced motion fully.

- Big map 1200x900 fixed but CSS scales? Fine.

- Audio is WebAudio procedural, no 3D spatialization. Not asked visual but relevant to modern standards maybe.
- No asset pipeline; generated at runtime. Suggest moving to GLB with Draco/meshopt, KTX2/Basis textures, baked lightmaps.

# BELLINGHAM: THE UNDERGROUND

An original, fully playable first-person open-world life sim and arcade fighting game set in a fictionalized Bellingham, Washington. Clock in, pay rent, fall in love, and try not to notice the city breathing back. Every stranger is a fighter. Every night is a round.

**18+.** Contains violence, crime, alcohol and drug themes, profanity, and psychological horror. Romance and intimacy are between consenting adults only, are non-graphic, and fade to black. There is no sexual violence or exploitation. All characters are adults. This is a work of fiction.

## Run it

No framework, no build step. The game is static HTML/CSS/JS with a locally vendored Three.js and local fonts.

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8123
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:8123/>. A modern desktop or mobile browser with WebGL is required.

On the hosted runtime, `start.sh` serves the project automatically.

## Controls

### On foot (keyboard + mouse)

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `W A S D` | Move |
| Mouse | Look |
| `Shift` | Sprint |
| `Ctrl` | Crouch |
| `Space` | Jump |
| `E` | Interact / talk |
| `Tab` | Phone |
| `M` | Map |
| `Esc` | Pause / close |

### Fighting

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `LMB` / `J` | Punch |
| `RMB` / `K` | Kick |
| `Q` | Block (hold) |
| `Space` | Dodge |
| `E` | Grapple |
| `R` | Special |
| `F` | Environmental attack |
| `C` | Finisher (when the meter is ready) |

### Driving

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `W` / `S` | Throttle / brake-reverse |
| `A` / `D` | Steer |
| `F` | Exit the car |

### Touch

Phones and tablets get a virtual stick, a look area, and context buttons for interact, jump, phone, sprint, and the full fight set (punch, kick, block, dodge, special). Touch controls respect safe areas and disable page gestures over the game surface.

## What is in the game

- **A living city.** Downtown, Fairhaven, Boulevard Park, the waterfront, WWU, Whatcom Falls, Lake Whatcom, Chuckanut, the marina, industrial lots, trails, and Mount Baker on the horizon. Rain, fog, storms, wet streets, traffic, pedestrians, wildlife, and a day/night cycle.
- **A life sim.** Jobs and shifts, rent and home ownership, food and cooking, sleep, hygiene, mood, gym training, bars, cafés, clubs, dating, relationships, clothing, hair, tattoos, vehicles, skills, reputation ranks, quests, and saving/loading.
- **A fighting game.** Ten named bosses, each with their own style and AI. Punch, kick, block, dodge, counter, grapple, combo, specials, environmental attacks, stamina, health, special meters, slow-motion finishers, and learnable fighting styles.
- **A story that starts normal.** The first shift is just a shift. Then the transit board flickers, a bus takes a road that was always there, and the city begins to stutter. The underground tournament is only the first layer.
- **The ten names:** THE BARISTA, THE FERRYMAN, THE HIKER, THE MECHANIC, THE STUDENT, THE OLD MAN AT THE PARK, THE RAINCOAT, THE MAYOR, THE MIRROR, and THE FUTURE PLAYER.
- **Hundreds of encounters.** 24 authored random events plus 480 procedurally generated street encounters, scaled by how much the simulation is glitching.
- **Artifacts, secrets, and alternate realities.** The brass token, the raincoat button, the mirror shard, the cassette. The Quiet Table. The thin door into the version of Bellingham that watches this one.
- **Five endings.** Escape, become champion, shut it down, take control, or stay. Requirements are tracked in the phone's journal. You can also ignore the tournament and live normally for as long as you like.

## Project layout

```text
index.html          DOM shell, HUD, menus, touch controls
styles.css          all layout and visual styling
src/main.js         orchestrator: state, story, jobs, phone, endings, input
src/world.js        procedural city, weather, arena, interactables
src/player.js       first-person movement, collision, driving, arms
src/npcs.js         NPC models, schedules, memory, ambient crowds
src/combat.js       fight loop, boss AI, meters, effects
src/ui.js           HUD, panels, dialogue, modal, map, combat UI
src/audio.js        procedural Web Audio music, rain, and SFX
src/data.js         characters, bosses, items, quests, events, styles
vendor/             local Three.js runtime
fonts/              local display and text fonts
```

Saves use `localStorage` under `bellingham_underground_save_v3`. The pause menu can erase a save.

## Notes

- All characters, businesses, art, music, dialogue, and events are original.
- The city is a fictionalized version of Bellingham, not a map of the real place.
- Built with Three.js (MIT) and locally bundled fonts. See the font licenses in `fonts/` and the vendored Three.js license in `vendor/`.

## 2. Graphics Upgrade Plan

### Direction

The current low-poly noir look is coherent and should **not** be replaced with photorealism. Target a **cinematic Pacific Northwest noir**: wet asphalt, sodium/teal neon, volumetric rain, heavy atmosphere, graphic UI. Think *Alan Wake 2* environments, *Control* institutional UI, *Disco Elysium* typography, and *Signalis* low-fi unease.

### Quality tiers

| Tier | Target | Textures | Shadows | Post |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PC High | 1440p–4K, 60 fps | 2K standard, 4K hero | 4 cascades, 2048–4096 | SSAO, SSR, bloom, volumetric fog, TAA |
| PC Mid / console | 1080p, 60 fps | 1–2K | 2 cascades, 2048 | SSAO, half-res SSR, bloom, SMAA |
| Mobile / web | 720–900p, 30–60 fps | 1K, 512 for props | 1 cascade, 1024 | baked AO, bloom only, no SSR |
| WebGPU path | 1080p, 60 fps | KTX2/Basis 1K | 1–2 cascades | lightweight AO + bloom + SMAA |

### Textures & materials

- **PBR metallic-roughness** everywhere: albedo, normal, ORM (AO/roughness/metallic), emissive.
- **2K** for modular buildings and props; **4K** only for hero close-ups, key signage, and UI backplates. Do not ship everything at 4K.
- **Trim sheets** for windows, doors, pipes, railings; **decals** for graffiti, posters, moss, water stains, road markings.
- **Wet-surface shader:** puddle mask, rain ripples, roughness breakup, darkened albedo, screen-space reflections.
- **Triplanar mapping** for terrain/cliffs; **parallax occlusion** for brick and siding.
- **Anisotropy 8–16**; mipmaps on; sRGB for albedo/emissive; linear for normal/ORM; BC7/ASTC compression; KTX2/Basis for web.

### Lighting

- Replace flat hemisphere lighting with **HDRI/IBL** (4K EXR → PMREM) plus a directional sun/moon.
- **Cascaded shadow maps**, 4 cascades on desktop, contact shadows for characters/props.
- **SSAO/GTAO**, **screen-space reflections** on wet roads, **light probes** for interiors and neon spill.
- **Volumetric height fog** and local fog cards; distant Mount Baker through atmospheric perspective.
- Emissive neon with bloom threshold ~0.9; restrained lens dirt and wet-lens droplets.
- Keep ACES/AgX tone mapping and exposure adaptation; grade toward crushed teal shadows and warm sodium highlights.

### Shaders & VFX

- Wet asphalt, puddle ripples, rain streaks, water with Fresnel/foam, glass with refraction, neon flicker.
- GPU rain, splash sprites, mist sheets, steam from vents, breath, impact debris, dust, paper blowing.
- Combat: hit sparks, rain displacement on impact, slow-motion finisher with DOF and chromatic aberration.
- Use decals for blood, scuffs, wet footprints; limit overdraw on mobile.

### Characters

- Hero characters: 20–35k triangles, 4-bone skinning, 2K textures, LODs, facial blendshapes.
- Crowd: 5–8k triangles, 1K atlas, 2 LODs, impostors at distance.
- Add cloth/hair cards, wet fabric sheen, raincoat clear-coat, and subtle idle motion.
- Keep the stylized proportions; upgrade silhouette and material response rather than realism.

### UI redesign

- Raise **minimum text size to 12px**, body 14px, titles 16–18px; 4/8px spacing grid.
- Keep the B//U mono/red/teal identity, but reduce simultaneous HUD elements; fade needs/controls contextually.
- Use a **diegetic phone** for journal, map, contacts; keep the HUD for immediate state only.
- WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1), focus states, controller/touch parity, safe-area support.
- Reduce `backdrop-filter` layers; use one blurred modal surface plus opaque cards.
- Honor `prefers-reduced-motion` for grain, glitch, shake, and camera bob.

### Performance budget

- 60 fps = 16.6 ms: ≤12 ms GPU, ≤4 ms CPU.
- Draw calls: <1,500 desktop, <400 mobile. Triangles: <2M desktop, <300k mobile.
- Texture memory: <2 GB desktop, <512 MB mobile.
- Use LODs, occlusion culling, GPU instancing, SRP Batcher/ Nanite where appropriate, and dynamic resolution.

---

## 3. Implementation Steps

The current build is **Three.js**, not Unity/Unreal. The practical sequence is: apply the web quick wins now, then port to Unity 6 HDRP or Unreal 5.4 if the target is a native release.

### Path A — Current Three.js build (fastest, lowest risk)

1. **Renderer:** keep ACES, enable `PCFSoftShadowMap`, 2048 desktop / 1024 mobile, `normalBias .025`; center the shadow camera on the player. *(Applied.)*
2. **Post stack:** add `EffectComposer` with `RenderPass`, `UnrealBloomPass`, N8AO/SSAO, `SMAAPass`, `OutputPass`; render at 0.75–1.0 resolution scale and upscale.
3. **IBL:** generate a PMREM environment from a 2K/4K storm HDRI; assign `scene.environment`; keep `scene.fog` for depth.
4. **Textures:** replace canvas facades with KTX2/Basis PBR atlases; set `anisotropy = 8`; add wetness/roughness maps.
5. **Rain:** replace CPU line-segment updates with a GPU vertex shader or instanced camera-facing quads; add splash decals.
6. **UI:** tokenized type scale, 12px minimum, reduce blur layers, add reduced-motion handling.
7. **Profiling:** Chrome Performance + WebGL Inspector; lock 60 fps, measure draw calls, shader compile spikes, and mobile thermal throttling.

### Path B — Unity 6 / HDRP

1. Create an **HDRP** project (Unity 6 LTS, HDRP 17), Linear color space, 16-bit HDR buffers.
2. Configure the HDRP Asset: **SSAO**, **Screen Space Reflections**, **Volumetric Fog**, **Decals**, **Contact Shadows**, **Bloom**, **Color Grading**, **Film Grain**, **Depth of Field**.
3. Lighting: physically based sky + 4K HDRI, directional sun with 4 cascades, 2048–4096 shadow atlas; reflection probes and light probes.
4. Materials: Shader Graph master shader with wetness, puddle mask, rain ripples, triplanar fallback; decals for grime and graffiti.
5. Assets: Blender → FBX/GLB, 1 unit = 1 m; PBR textures 2K, BC7/ASTC; LOD Groups; Addressables; occlusion culling; GPU instancing; SRP Batcher.
6. VFX: VFX Graph for rain, splashes, mist, steam, impact; Shuriken only for simple one-shots.
7. UI: UI Toolkit + TextMeshPro; 12/14/16px scale; safe-area handling; Input System for controller/touch.
8. Plugins: Cinemachine, Addressables, DLSS/FSR/XeSS, Unity Profiler/Frame Debugger.
9. Performance: 16.6 ms budget, shadow atlas limits, texture streaming, dynamic resolution, LOD bias tuning.

### Path C — Unreal Engine 5.4

1. Enable **Lumen GI/reflections**, **Nanite** for modular buildings, **Virtual Shadow Maps**, **TSR**, **World Partition**, **HLOD**, **PCG** for street clutter.
2. Use **Sky Atmosphere**, **Volumetric Clouds**, **Exponential Height Fog**, and a 4K HDRI for the noir sky.
3. Build a PBR master material with wetness, puddle, rain-ripple, clear-coat, and triplanar parameters; use **Runtime Virtual Textures** for road wetness and decals.
4. Add a Post Process Volume: bloom, exposure, color grading LUT, film grain, vignette, DOF, restrained chromatic aberration.
5. Niagara for rain, splashes, mist, steam, and combat impacts; MetaSounds for spatial rain/neon hum.
6. UMG/CommonUI for the phone/HUD; 12px minimum, controller focus, safe zones.
7. Import pipeline: 2K/4K PBR, Oodle, texture streaming pool, Nanite fallback meshes, collision primitives, LODs for non-Nanite assets.
8. Performance: DLSS/FSR/XeSS, VSM page pool, Lumen scene detail, HLOD, streaming budgets; target 1080p60 mid-range, 1440p60 high-end.

---

content.text:
AddStrip uses a box scaled; texture UVs are per-face 0-1, so a texture would stretch across the entire 420m strip. Need repeat based on size. Options:
- Use a plane with geometry subdivided and set UV repeat per material clone (texture.repeat.set(w/4, d/4)). Cloning texture per strip (26 strips) is okay, but each clone uploads same image? Three.js clones share image, so one upload per texture object? Each Texture clone has its own GPU texture upload (same image but separate texture). 26 × 256² = manageable (26*256KB ≈ 6.7MB). But we can reuse two materials and rely on world-space UV via custom shader? Simpler: create a **single road material with a texture whose repeat is large**, but each strip has different dimensions → stretched differently.

Better approach: use a custom shader material or modify UVs on a per-strip basis. Since box geometry is shared, we can instead create a plane geometry per strip with UVs scaled to world units:
```
const geo = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(w, d, 1, 1);
geo.rotateX(-PI/2);
const uv = geo.attributes.uv;
for i: uv.setXY(i, uv.getX(i)*w/4, uv.getY(i)*d/4);
```
Then use a shared material with map.wrapS/T = RepeatWrapping and repeat 1. That tiles every 4m. This is clean. Replace addStrip to use PlaneGeometry (slightly above terrain, no thickness needed) — but the box currently has thickness .06 and sides; planes are fine for ground. 60: ## What is in the game
61: 
62: - **A living city.** Downtown, Fairhaven, Boulevard Park, the waterfront, WWU, Whatcom Falls, Lake Whatcom, Chuckanut, the marina, industrial lots, trails, and Mount Baker on the horizon. Rain, fog, storms, wet streets, traffic, pedestrians, wildlife, and a day/night cycle.
63: - **A life sim.** Jobs and shifts, rent and home ownership, food and cooking, sleep, hygiene, mood, gym training, bars, cafés, clubs, dating, relationships, clothing, hair, tattoos, vehicles, skills, reputation ranks, quests, and saving/loading.
64: - **A fighting game.** Ten named bosses, each with their own style and AI. Punch, kick, block, dodge, counter, grapple, combo, specials, environmental attacks, stamina, health, special meters, slow-motion finishers, and learnable fighting styles.
65: - **A story that starts normal.** The first shift is just a shift. Then the transit board flickers, a bus takes a road that was always there, and the city begins to stutter. The underground tournament is only the first layer.
66: - **The ten names:** THE BARISTA, THE FERRYMAN, THE HIKER, THE MECHANIC, THE STUDENT, THE OLD MAN AT THE PARK, THE RAINCOAT, THE MAYOR, THE MIRROR, and THE FUTURE PLAYER.
67: - **Hundreds of encounters.** 24 authored random events plus 480 procedurally generated street encounters, scaled by how much the simulation is glitching.
68: - **Artifacts, secrets, and alternate realities.** The brass token, the raincoat button, the mirror shard, the cassette. The Quiet Table. The thin door into the version of Bellingham that watches this one.
69: - **Five endings.** Escape, become champion, shut it down, take control, or stay. Requirements are tracked in the phone's journal. You can also ignore the tournament and live normally for as long as you like.
